solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Harrow for the first time to be innovative

definitions.meaning: harrowing breaks up soil, and doing it first means ground nobody has broken before
the figurative sense: to do something nobody has done

explanation.walkthrough: To harrow is to break up ploughed soil, so doing it for the first time is literally breaking new ground; the figurative sense is doing something no one has done before.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: an idiom for pioneering, and taken literally the first pass of a harrow over untouched soil.

clue.text: Start to read publication holding new version

indicators.note: 'start to read' asks for the first letter of 'read'

parts.note: first letter of 'read'

indicators.note: the publication holds the new letter inside it

parts.note: an edition is one publication of a paper or book
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone begins reading a newspaper that carries a fresh version of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: N goes just after the first letter of EDITION, and the R from 'read' sits in front of the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a version or performance of something, as of a song.

clue.text: Fit silver on table at last

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
re means on or about, as in a memo

indicators.note: 'table at last' points to the final letter of 'table'

parts.note: last letter of 'table'

explanation.surface: Someone checks whether the silverware fits when it is finally laid on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' reads as a position word in the surface, but here it is RE, meaning about.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that agree fit or match each other, as a story fits the facts.

clue.text: Wrought iron panel that's unmatched

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters of 'iron panel' are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A craftsman boasts of a wrought-iron panel that has no equal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrought iron' looks like one fixed phrase, but 'wrought' is working on its own on 'iron panel'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nonpareil comes from French for 'without equal', so it means unmatched.

clue.text: Comedian, extremely envious, demands payment

definitions.note: WAGES is plural; the singular 'payment' stands for pay in general

parts.note: a wag is a joker or wit

indicators.note: 'extremely envious' takes only the extremes, the first and last letters, of 'envious'

parts.note: first and last letters of 'envious'

explanation.surface: A jealous comic insists on getting paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' belongs to the letters, not the envy: it keeps only the E and S of 'envious'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what an employer hands over for work, usually spoken of in the plural.

clue.text: Online merchant recalled accepting thanks in reply

indicators.note: the turned merchant accepts, or takes in, the thanks
to recall is to call back, so the merchant comes back to front

parts.note: an e-tailer is an online retailer
ta is British informal for thanks

explanation.surface: A web shop, asked to take back goods, answers with a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: E-tailer is a modern coinage for a web shop, and it must be turned round before the thanks goes in, just after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To retaliate is to reply in kind, hitting back at an attack.

clue.text: Man having time to find employment

parts.note: man as humankind is us, the human race
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A man takes his time about getting a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' reads as one fellow, but it means mankind, which is all of us.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage is the employment of something, the way it is used.

clue.text: Doctor sees wounded duke bandaged

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: wounded letters are damaged and out of shape

parts.note: anagram fodder, 4 letters
D is the abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A doctor examines an injured duke, who is then bandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wounded' works twice in the surface, but in the wordplay it only scrambles SEES.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressed wound has had a dressing, a bandage, put on it.

clue.text: Economies elevated firm producing fine plaster

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it from bottom to top

parts.note: cuts are economies, savings
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A company making cutbacks still manages to turn out good plaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elevated firm' seems to go together, but 'elevated' belongs to 'Economies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster used to coat walls and make mouldings.

clue.text: All fingers and thumbs — or finding settled course

parts.note: eight fingers and two thumbs make ten
used as printed

explanation.surface: A clumsy person tries to find a steady path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All fingers and thumbs' means clumsy in British English, but here it is counted literally: ten.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenor of something is its settled course or general drift.

clue.text: With REM, a thing to disturb?

definitions.text: With REM, a thing to disturb?

indicators.note: disturbed letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: anagram fodder, 9 letters

explanation.surface: A question about what comes during REM sleep to trouble the sleeper.
explanation.walkthrough: REM is rapid eye movement, the dream phase of sleep, so the whole clue also describes a nightmare.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightmare is a disturbing dream, and dreams come in REM sleep.

clue.text: Monster to agree with hawk- headed god

parts.note: to chime with something is to agree with it
Ra is the Egyptian sun god, shown with a hawk's head

explanation.surface: A monster sides with an Egyptian bird-headed deity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two pieces, so CHIME is followed by RA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chimera is a fire-breathing monster of Greek myth, part lion, goat and serpent.

clue.text: Retailers, clairvoyants accepting Liberal line

indicators.note: the clairvoyants accept, or take in, the two Ls

parts.note: seers see the future
L is the abbreviation for Liberal
L is the abbreviation for line

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers and fortune-tellers fall in with the Liberal party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' reads as the party line, but it is just another L to go with the Liberal one.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shops and traders who deal with the public exist to sell things.

clue.text: One with hesitation joins operation to find narcotic

indicators.note: the one-with-hesitation pair joins on after the operation, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: op is short for operation
I is the Roman numeral one
um is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A hesitant person signs up for a police raid on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue lists the pieces out of order; OP comes first, then I with its UM.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the dried poppy latex is the original narcotic, the source of morphine.

clue.text: Counter in music shop?

parts.note: not a sales desk but something that counts, here musical beats
where you would buy one

explanation.walkthrough: The counter seems to be the shop's sales desk, but it is a device that counts beats for musicians.
explanation.definitionFit: A metronome ticks out the beat, counting time for a player, and music shops sell them.

clue.text: Described grassland appearing in river delta

indicators.note: the grassland appears inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
a plain is open grassland
D is delta in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone describes grassland spreading across a river delta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'River delta' looks like one place, but the delta is just the letter D tacked on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the past tense: both mean set something out in words so others understand it.

clue.text: Sensible MP with a tragic undoing

indicators.note: undoing the letters pulls them apart for rebuilding

parts.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A level-headed politician meets a tragic downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' ties MP to 'a tragic', and all nine letters get rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: dealing with things practically, as they are, rather than by theory or ideals.

clue.text: Managed to get raise with share account

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word writes it upward

parts.note: to run a business is to manage it
a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: A worker wangled a pay rise and a share account.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise' sounds like a pay rise, but it turns RAN upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the telling of a story, as a narrator gives it, is an account of events.

clue.text: Headless insect found in dish that's smoked

definitions.note: a clause for a thing that is smoked, standing for the noun

indicators.note: a headless word loses its first letter
the insect is found inside the dish

parts.note: paella is a Spanish rice dish
GNAT without its head, G

explanation.surface: A decapitated bug turns up in a plate of smoked food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoked' looks like it describes the dish, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A panatella is a long thin cigar, something that is smoked.

clue.text: Expert thus securing a flat

parts.note: a pro is an expert

indicators.note: thus secures, or holds, the A inside it

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus
used as printed

explanation.surface: A property expert helps someone buy a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A flat' reads as an apartment, but the A goes into SIC and 'flat' means dull.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosaic means flat and unimaginative, like plain prose.

clue.text: Bird plunged into water gets back

indicators.note: the letters are read back, right to left
the bird is plunged inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters straddle the two words and are taken from right to left

explanation.surface: A bird dives into water and then gets back out.
explanation.walkthrough: Run backward, 'water gets' reads STEGRETAW, with EGRET in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a white wading bird of the heron family.

clue.text: Non-drinker involved in row causing giggle

indicators.note: the non-drinker is caught up inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
TT means teetotal, someone who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A sober person caught up in an argument makes people laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel, but here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short, half-stifled laugh.

clue.text: Chapel area in gold and blue

indicators.note: the area goes in between gold and blue

parts.note: or is gold in heraldry
A is the abbreviation for area
blue is the colour of the Tories, Britain's Conservative party

explanation.surface: Part of a chapel is decorated in gold and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold and blue' reads as a colour scheme, but gold is the heraldic word and blue is political, with the area set between them.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratory is a small chapel for private prayer.

clue.text: Union Station?

parts.note: a union of two people in marriage
the place where that union is made

explanation.walkthrough: Union Station is a railway terminus name in many US cities; here the union is a marriage and the station is where it happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A couple is joined in marriage standing at the altar.

clue.text: Froth on beer indeed soft at the edges

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes, indeed

indicators.note: the edges of 'soft' are its first and last letters

parts.note: first and last letters of 'soft'

explanation.surface: The head on a pint really is soft around the rim.
explanation.walkthrough: YEA is an old word for yes, used here to mean 'indeed'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary sense: the frothy barm that rises on fermenting beer is itself the living yeast.

clue.text: Wandering Russian fighter encounters storm

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet
to storm is to rant angrily

explanation.surface: A Russian warplane off course runs into bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like weather, but it is angry shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Migrant as an adjective means wandering from place to place.

clue.text: Go round city and finally ask for wall sticker?

indicators.note: 'round' in its sense of around: GO wraps itself around the city and the final letter of 'ask'

parts.note: used as printed
EC is the postcode of the City of London

indicators.note: 'finally ask' is the last letter of 'ask'

parts.note: last letter of 'ask'

explanation.surface: Someone tours a city and then asks for a sticker for the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a playful definition: a wall sticker sounds like a decal, but it is a lizard.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos have sticky toe pads that let them cling to walls.

clue.text: Space traveller's American out to Saturn

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for American

indicators.note: letters put out are knocked out of place

parts.note: anagram fodder, 8 letters

explanation.surface: An American space traveller heads out to Saturn.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s is short for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word is Greek for star sailor, the standard name for anyone who travels into space.

clue.text: Companion brought to French island nation

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British order
île is French for island

explanation.surface: A companion is taken to an island nation off France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Island nation' seems to go together, but the island is ILE and 'nation' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: one of many nations, the long thin one on South America's Pacific coast.

clue.text: Ready source for story in the news

definitions.meaning: ready is British slang for cash, so this is the bank account you draw money from day to day
a report on what is happening right now

explanation.walkthrough: A current account is the British name for a checking account, a ready source of cash; read literally, it is a current, topical account or story.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the British banking term for an everyday account, and read literally an up-to-date report.
